status.question: Does a trust-region fit that uses a neural surrogate as its model, corrected at each centre with the NGSpice value and Jacobian, reach direct-NGSpice accuracy with fewer NGSpice calls? Thesis under test: neural surrogates do not rank candidate cards in the order NGSpice ranks them, and inverse networks trained on simulations have large errors on measured devices (model misspecification).

answer.text: Same search with NGSpice in place of the surrogate, 43 parameters, round 1: all-device RRMS 0.2382 → 0.1125 (combined 0.2289 → 0.1053). The pipeline value is from its final selection rerun with the same surrogate and the rule that rejects candidates with failed included curves; 18 of 18 devices are valid. Before the fix the stored pipeline value was 0.2375, with 1 failed device (0.2395 over the 17 valid devices, 0.2920 penalized).

The round-1 43-parameter surrogate orders its own picks and the direct-fit cards opposite to NGSpice on 16 of 18 devices (surrogate 0.2474 vs 0.5074; NGSpice 0.2382 vs 0.1269, all-device), with the picks from the final selection rerun with failed-curve rejection. With the picks made before the fix the count was 17 of 18 (surrogate 0.2034; NGSpice 0.2375 stored, 1 device with a failed included curve).

Six surrogate architectures in the same search, 43 parameters, round 1: end-to-end all-device RRMS 0.2274–0.2549 vs 0.1125 with NGSpice in place of the surrogate; the lowest test loss (FNO) has the highest end-to-end RRMS. Diagnostic ablation on the measured devices, not used for method selection.
Tandem inverse network (A), seven parameters: median device RRMS 0.0258 on held-out simulated devices, 0.6344 on measured devices.
Hybrid trust-region fit: DEV results at 500–5000 calls on 36 targets are in [dev-iter1](#claim-dev-iter1).

items.name: n1a · sketched Jacobians
items.method: At each trust-region centre, k = 8 directional NGSpice probes (Gauss-Newton step, top singular vectors of the transported prior, one Gaussian direction) plus secant and Broyden updates replace the 43-call FD Jacobian; a full FD Jacobian at the first centre, on refresh, and on prior mismatch. Control: the same code with no surrogate.

items.name: Hermite discrepancy correction
items.method: Multi-centre gradient-enhanced (Hermite) GP correction of the surrogate-NGSpice discrepancy, first-order consistent at the centre, using every NGSpice call including rejected trials. Proposed in iteration 1 and not selected for implementation.

items.name: n1c · CMA-ES call-trace baseline
items.method: CMA-ES (sigma0 0.3, popsize 15) then bounded TRF, and lq-CMA-ES, on the same oracle, bank start, objective and call accounting as the trust-region arms, with an exact trace of best RRMS against cumulative NGSpice calls.

items.name: n1b · anytime racing
items.method: Eight zero-call surrogate presearch starts, racing of trust-region runs by predicted reduction per NGSpice call, optimistic-bound drops, surrogate-proposed restarts.

what: Question: how much of the paper pipeline's error at 43 parameters comes from the surrogate rather than from the search procedure?

Paper pipeline (cold, round 1): a 10k-card Latin-hypercube bank per device in the round-1 box, simulated in NGSpice; a forward surrogate (parameters → I–V) trained on it from random initialization; 8 diverse bank starts; bounded TRF least squares on the surrogate with 2-point FD (max_nfev 100, diff_step 0.02, regularization 1e-4); NGSpice validation of the top 4 endpoints, the 4 starts and the fallback.

Result files written before the fix keep their stored values; `out/research/audit/failed_curves.json` recomputes the three values for 227 runs, 16 of which have a failed device.

what: Question: does a different or larger surrogate architecture, trained on the same data with the same recipe, change the end-to-end result of the pipeline's search on the measured devices?

Architectures (`src/cryoml/operators.py`): paper MLP (4 × 1024 hidden, 5.3M trainable parameters), wide MLP (6 × 2048, 25.3M), residual MLP (27.3M), large residual MLP (138.6M), DeepONet (branch residual MLP, trunk over the bias point, 25.8M) and an FNO conditioned along each curve's sweep axis (4.1M).

Fixed across architectures: the round-1 43-parameter cache (`out/cold_loop/full/round_1/cache`); the per-device train/validation/test split of the pipeline (seed 20260818, 85,853 training samples); the loss (standardized signed-log MSE + curve-normalized linear Huber); the recipe (AdamW, cosine schedule, early stopping on validation loss, at most 200 epochs, FNO at most 80); and the search (`fps.finite_difference_surrogate_extract`: 8 starts, TRF max_nfev 100, diff_step 0.02, regularization 1e-4, NGSpice validation of the top 4 endpoints, the first 4 starts and the published fallback).

Measured per architecture: test loss and curve NRMSE on held-out bank samples; surrogate-predicted and NGSpice RRMS of three reference card sets (the stored pipeline r1 picks, direct NGSpice cold, direct NGSpice seeded); and the end-to-end search on the 18 measured devices, each selected card re-simulated in NGSpice.
